literature_notes: All ten ledger clips (L1–L10) describe N-terminal SNAP-tag or FLAG-tag fusions to CLDN4. The authoritative topology landmarks place the CLDN4 N-terminus (residues 1–9) in the intracellular compartment; there is no signal peptide. A tag prepended before M1 (insert_after_residue=0) therefore sits on the cytoplasmic face, not the extracellular surface. The papers describe these constructs as 'surface-expressed' or 'surface-displayed', meaning the full-length protein traffics correctly to the plasma membrane — not that the N-terminal tag is accessible from the extracellular space. No ledger clip reports a tag insertion in ECL1 (residues 31–81) or ECL2 (residues 138–160), the only extracellular loops. L7 additionally reports that FLAG-Cldn4 fails to form a paracellular barrier when expressed in TJ-deficient cells, indicating functional perturbation of the construct. Because no ledger line grounds an extracellular surface tag site, the correct answer is zero qualifying sites.

literature_other_positions.note: SNAP tag inserted at the amino terminus of endogenous CLDN4 via CRISPR knock-in; the N-terminus (residues 1–9) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag is on the cytoplasmic face, not the extracellular surface.
FLAG tag introduced at the N-terminus of Cldn4 by PCR with a forward primer encoding FLAG before the start codon; same intracellular N-terminus as above.
